data.title: 'Pragmatic international relations': Sánchez seeks to avoid 'further conflict with Rabat'
data.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Alana Moceri, International Relations Professor at IE School of Politics, Economics and Global Affairs. The migrant crossings at Ceuta have become both a domestic and international political lightning rod. At home, Pedro Sánchez faces opponents who can cast migration in existential terms, with Spain's far right amplifying the rhetoric of "invasion." Internationally, the crisis exposes the geopolitical leverage inherent in control of the border. Ceuta thus emerges as more than a migration crisis: the border becomes at once an instrument of geopolitical leverage, a weapon in Spain's domestic political contest, and a battleground for competing narratives and disinformation.

data.title: ‘Why not try to be the best in the world, just for the fun of it?’ Art Garfunkel on a rich, restless life – and reconciling with Paul Simon
data.description: He taught maths and walked across Europe, trying to leave his demons behind. As he goes back on tour aged 83, the folk-pop legend explains how he came back to singing As Art Garfunkel is keen to point out, “I am a singer – there, use that as the title of your article” – but he was never just a singer. “I’ve been an actor. I am a writer,” he continues. “I’ve walked across countries, taken freighters across oceans. I’ve read the dictionary. I’ve read two books a month for 60 years: Darwin, Herodotus, Balzac, Proust, Tolstoy. I’ve taught maths. I have two great kids and I’m a grandfather, but it always does seem to come back to the singing.” Which is understandable, given that in Simon and Garfunkel (with songwriter Paul Simon) he sold more albums than any other pop duo in history. Garfunkel’s oft-called “angelic” tones powered classic chart-toppers including The Sound of Silence and Bridge Over Troubled Water, and he became a successful solo artist. However, until a year ago, he was hardly singing at all and hadn’t toured since 2019. “I found myself lying on a pillow in a dream state, thinking about the meaning of being alive,” he reveals. “What is my day? What am I supposed to do with myself?” Continue reading...

data.title: Experience: I didn’t know I was pregnant until I gave birth
data.description: There’d been no morning sickness, cravings or tiredness. My mum didn’t believe I’d had a baby – even after seeing her on FaceTime When I was 19, I went to college in Texas, where I met my ­boyfriend Preston. It was 2023 and I had big plans. After ­finishing my degree in criminal justice, I wanted to go to law school. I wasn’t in a rush to get married or have kids. My mum had drilled into me a fear of getting pregnant at a young age. I was on the pill and careful with contraception. In May 2025, I took a trip to London, returning to campus in August after the summer holidays. I noticed I was slowly gaining weight; by January this year I’d gained 10lb. I put it down to my late-night snacking and lack of exercise. Continue reading...

data.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
data.description: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”. She spent much of her life on the road, often accompanied by equally committed fellow campaigners. Steinem loathed public speaking, but during two years travelling in India in her 20s, she moved from village to village, with “a sari, a cup and a comb” in a group countering religious intolerance. She said she learned then, as Gandhi taught, that a message was all the more powerful delivered “eye to eye”. Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion. Continue reading...

data.title: The Ceuta border breach was leapt on by Europe’s right. That doesn’t absolve Spain | María Ramírez
data.description: The government’s sluggish response has been disastrous for everyone involved – and for Sánchez’s message on immigration More than a month after an estimated 72,000 people suddenly crossed from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, the city remains in chaos and the damage inflicted on the Spanish government is becoming clearer. Most of those who made the crossing have returned to Morocco. The scale of the incident was nevertheless extraordinary, and about 140 people are thought to have died . Also extraordinary was the response of the 22 EU governments that rounded on the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, rather than demonstrate the solidarity one might expect from allies. Perhaps less surprising was the exploitation of the crisis by rightwing and far-right parties in Spain and beyond, Donald Trump’s attacks and the interventions of Russian state-linked actors and Israeli critics on social media to fuel division . Continue reading...

data.title: The Bayeux tapestry: a stupefying, thrilling, horrifying masterpiece that shakes the earth
data.description: British Museum, London The greatest battle ever depicted in art is here at last – and it hurtles along, making your heart pound with its sense of doom and destiny, culminating in fires and corpses on a battlefield full of pathos It should not work. It should not even exist. Nothing about the Bayeux tapestry makes sense according to any norms of art: its creators couldn’t do proper portraits or pictorial depth or landscapes or any of the sophisticated things we associate with timeless masterpieces. When they depict a church, they have to write what it is: Ecclesia. But these artists – or who knows, perhaps she was a single artist – created something so stupefying and delightful, so abundant in visual thrills, horrors and humour, it beats almost everything else ever painted or carved – let alone embroidered on a strip of linen. And now here it is, in front of my eyes, close enough to touch if it wasn’t behind a glass screen of such high quality you never catch a reflection. The British Museum’s display of this wonder is perfect. It’s laid out in its case, the length of a gallery, which you reach after some archaeological foreplay involving armour, quotes from chronicles and info screens. Then you see the colours of the tapestry below you from a parapet – russets, greens, yellows – after which you simply start at the beginning and follow the story rightwards. Surrounded by darkness and picked out by finely adjusted lighting, the Bayeux tapestry shines. My only quibble is the ethereal soundtrack – shouldn’t there be drums, oliphants, troubadours? Continue reading...

data.title: Nessun Dolore review – sketchy Roman fable of liberal white guilt
data.description: Venice film festival A white man’s eyes are opened to cruelty and racism when a young boy is thrust into his life in Gianni Amelio’s bold but ultimately naive drama From the heart of Rome, and broadly in an Italian tradition of sentimentalist realism, film-maker Gianni Amelio brings us a fairytale of the city, about the liberal white guilt of those who live a prosperous pain-free existence and those whom Frantz Fanon called the wretched of the earth. There is some incidental interest and the film is beautifully shot, but finally it buckles under the weight of its own preposterousness and naivety. It is also sketchy about how and why people go into and come out of prison; the final shot, a supposedly heartwarming visionary moment of redemption and reconciliation, looks absurd. data.title: ‘If you can’t understand what sex is, it’s irrelevant if you seem to be enjoying it’: how Queen at Sea upended the dementia drama
data.description: Lance Hammer’s first film in 18 years is a heart-wrenching masterpiece about family, mental decline and sexual consent. He and supporting actor Juliette Binoche discuss how they brought unabashed realism to a condition rarely seen on screen The first time we see Martin and Leslie, the elderly couple at the centre of Lance Hammer’s wrenching new film, Queen at Sea, they are walking together up a set of stone steps: one of their regular outings, we assume, in days filled with pottering and quiet companionship. They have their backs to us, and we can’t see their destination beyond a bleached sky that fills the top half of the screen. Symbolically, it may be deemed a bit on the nose: two people near the end of their lives, moving gently towards the white light of oblivion. There’s a whiff of sentimentality about it. But any doubts about this story’s willingness to confront difficult truths are blasted away by the next scene. Leslie’s daughter, Amanda, played by Juliette Binoche, pays a visit to the couple’s house in drizzly, middle-class north London, her teenage daughter in tow. Unable to find her mother and stepfather, she arrives at the bedroom door. Opening it, she finds Martin (Tom Courtenay) on top of Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall), who lies impassively beneath him, the mask of dementia obvious on her face. Continue reading...

data.title: The Golden Hours by Louisa Young review – this continuation of the Cazalet Chronicles is a total delight
data.description: Elizabeth Jane Howard’s niece has picked up the thread of her much-loved family saga series, taking the story into the 1960s Elizabeth Jane Howard’s beloved family saga the Cazalet Chronicles spans three decades in the life of the upper-middle-class Cazalet family. The first four books, written in the 1990s, run from a bucolic prewar 1937 to a bruising 1947, while the fifth, 2013’s All Change , skips ahead, sitting lonely in 1956. The books are exquisite doll’s houses of feeling and object: both period detail and eternal emotion are rendered precisely and vigorously in Howard’s lovely prose. “Panoramic, expansive, intriguing as social history and generous in their storytelling,” Hilary Mantel wrote in the Guardian . The enormous cast of characters – four late-Victorian siblings, their parents, their children and partners and ex-partners and servants and friends and lovers and enemies and cars and houses – sprawl deliciously over the years. The family fortunes rise and fall. Marriages fail; deaths occur; babies are born; people fall in love. Things change; things stay the same. Written a decade after the death of the original author, The Golden Hours by Louisa Young adds a sixth to this quintet. As with all Cazalet novels, to describe the plot would be impossible: it is simply that many people, whom we have come to love over the course of the previous novels, live their lives, now in the early 1960s. Continue reading...

data.title: For Ukraine's artists, making sense of rage is a necessity: it can be both requiem and resistance | Charlotte Higgins
data.description: Literature shows us how anger can inspire but also consume us: I see it in Homer’s epics, and in the furious creativity of contemporary Ukrainian writers Twice, I have heard Ukrainians perform Verdi’s Requiem. Once in Lviv , last Maundy Thursday, and once last month, under the great dome of St Paul’s Cathedral in London. In St Paul’s , performed by the Ukrainian Freedom Orchestra with the Philharmonia Chorus, the great Dies irae – “day of anger” – unfurled in an operatic gale of fury, reverberating so powerfully around Wren’s lofty spaces that the music felt like thunder echoing between mountain peaks. In Lviv, where it was performed by a Ukrainian chorus and orchestra, the evening began with a call to remember the war dead. Lviv’s lay a mile up the road: 153 graves when I first visited in autumn 2022, and by this year more than 1,000. Ranks and ranks of soldiers killed in their 20s, 30s and 40s, each grave planted with flowers and plants, flags flying above. On that occasion, Dies irae – in the more sober acoustic of the Lviv Philharmonic Hall – seemed to contain the furious ache of grief. Certainly I have never heard a more wrathful day of anger. Continue reading...

data.title: Gloria Steinem personified America’s feminist movement | Moira Donegan
data.description: The activist made the movement mainstream – and became a receptacle for its hopes and disappointments Gloria Steinem, groundbreaking feminist campaigner, dies aged 92 ‘We badly need to raise our boys more like our girls’: Gloria Steinem – a life in quotes By the time she died on Wednesday, at 92 years old at her home in New York, Gloria Steinem was synonymous with feminism, a kind of human mascot for the movement. So it can be easy to forget that when she was born, feminism was over. It was something that had been faddish years before, among women who were now old ladies; something that seemed, in retrospect, like it might have been a bit overwrought and out of touch. To the girl Gloria Steinem, growing up in Ohio in the 1930s and 40s, the suffrage movement that had gained women the right to vote less than two decades prior probably seemed remote – especially to a girl like her, growing up itinerant and poor under the care of a single mother who was plagued by a violent and debilitating mental illness. You might say that growing up, Steinem had worries that were more immediate than the status of women. But experience has a way of radicalizing women about their own gendered condition. Steinem attended Smith, and her education opened up previously unhoped for possibilities. En route to a postgraduate fellowship in India in 1957, when she was in her early 20s, she had an illegal abortion in London. Later, in 1969, while she was working as a journalist for New York magazine, she attended an “abortion speak-out” put on by a group of radical women from the emergent fringe of what was then called the Women’s Liberation movement. Continue reading...

data.title: The wars in Ukraine and Iran are becoming dangerously enmeshed | Christopher S Chivvis
data.description: As the Trump administration refuses to end its war in Iran, it is steering into the storm, not out of it Russia hasn’t yet killed large numbers of Europeans outside Ukraine, but it’s getting closer. The night of 4-5 August, an airport bus driver discovered an armed drone lying near the tarmac of the Leipzig-Halle airport, which is a central hub of Europe’s logistical support to Ukraine’s war effort. A cargo jet, meanwhile, may have struck a second drone shortly after takeoff, forcing an abrupt landing, and investigators found a third drone laden with military explosives nearby. In 2024, incendiary devices hidden in parcels ignited in DHL cargo at the same airport. Had these detonated in the air, a major air catastrophe and large-scale civilian casualties would have ensued, probably resulting in a broader war. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Capitalism is dying’: in Luton, these former car workers have a moral tale for our times | Aditya Chakrabortty
data.description: Abandoned by the company they worked for, let down by Labour and their unions – now they watch their friends turn to Reform for answers After everything, why would anyone still back Nigel Farage? In some of the comments below my piece last week about Reform UK, I spot the usual answers: Farage’s supporters are dim, racist, deplorable. Yet away from Westminster and the news cycle, Reform voters are being manufactured – not with headlines or crypto funds but through the failure of institutions they once trusted to protect them. To see what I mean, leave SW1 and go 40 miles up the road, to Luton. In a deserted hotel bar, five men are reminiscing about how their world ended. Their minds are on a Friday afternoon in March last year, as the place where they had worked for two or three decades apiece, making friends and even meeting future wives, is about to shut for good. data.title: The Guardian view on press freedom: to defend democracy, stand up for journalists | Editorial
data.description: The lack of justice for Daphne Caruana Galizia in Malta casts a shadow on reporters everywhere The acquittal of Yorgen Fenech , who was on trial in Malta for involvement in the murder of the journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, is a devastating blow for justice and press freedom. Nine years after her car was blown up, it seems increasingly unlikely that anyone will be held to account for ordering and paying for her death. Mr Fenech’s admissions that he knew about the murder before it happened, and gave money to the middle-man who paid the killers, make it hard to understand why he was found not guilty on the lesser charge of association. All killings of journalists are wrong. The bomb placed in Caruana Galizia’s car was especially shocking, as such brazen violence is usually associated with war zones or states overrun by organised crime. The fact that this acquittal came two months after those of three men accused of murdering another journalist , Lyra McKee, in Northern Ireland, adds to a grim impression of impunity for killers. While McKee is not thought to have been targeted in the way that Caruana Galizia was, the inability of police and prosecutors to secure convictions in either case points to wider problems. data.title: The Guardian view on Nigeria’s kidnappings: a country can’t prosper when going to school is a danger | Editorial
data.description: Abductions are resurging and may be spreading to new areas – with young children among the victims. A military response alone won’t work Early last month, Nigeria’s government announced the largest single-day hostage rescue in its history, with the freeing of 300 people who had been taken in raids in two north central states. Celebrations were short-lived. Barely a fortnight later, gunmen abducted up to 600 worshippers from a mosque in Niger state. Nigerians paid kidnappers nearly $6m in ransoms in the year to June, according to a new report from the Lagos-based consultancy SBM Intelligence – more than triple the total in the previous 12-month period. More than 7,800 people were abducted, a two-thirds increase, and more than 1,100 killed, including almost 900 civilians. When Boko Haram abducted almost 300 schoolgirls from their school in Chibok, Borno state in 2014, it made headlines worldwide. Yet around 45 children, mostly aged between two and five, remain missing after they were snatched from schools in Mussa , in north-eastern Borno state, in May. There is growing concern that kidnappings may be spreading to new areas. Forty-six students and staff were abducted from three schools in the south-western state of Oyo in the same month; they were rescued in July. data.title: Andy Ruiz Jr once turned boxing upside down. Can he do it again at 36?
data.description: Seven years after springing one of the biggest upsets in boxing history, the Mexican Rocky is back with his old trainer for one final run at the heavyweight summit Seven years ago, Andy Ruiz Jr became the first fighter of Mexican descent to win the world heavyweight championship in one of the biggest upsets boxing has ever seen, stopping the undefeated Anthony Joshua inside seven rounds at Madison Square Garden. A replacement opponent summoned on five weeks’ notice who went off as an 11-1 underdog, Ruiz came off the canvas in the third to knock Joshua down four times before the referee finally waved it off. Hailed as the “Mexican Rocky”, he was lionized as a border-straddling hero in his hometown of Imperial, the dusty agricultural community framed by the mountain ranges and flat deserts of south-eastern California. He made the late-night rounds , took an audience with Mexico president Andrés Manuel López Obrador and signed a $10m guarantee when Joshua activated his rematch clause. The money, cars, fame and women arrived all at once. Continue reading...

We definitely don’t want this gas spewing needlessly into the atmosphere, but in 2023 that’s exactly what environment editor Damian Carrington found was happening when he reported on 1,000 super-emitting methane leaks across the globe. Now Turkmenistan, the worst country for mega-leaks, has begun to plug them. Damian tells Madeleine Finlay why some experts call stopping leaks the climate ‘emergency brake’ and reveals which countries are still failing to act. Continue reading...

data.title: La Mesías review – this utterly bizarre TV show is unforgettable
data.description: Finally landing on Mubi, this Spanish mega-hit about six sisters drilled into becoming viral Christian pop stars is wildly ambitious, blackly funny and a true triumph. Oh, and there are UFOs too At Primavera Sound festival in Barcelona in 2024, nestled alongside the likes of Pulp and Charli xcx was an unusual addition to the bill. Stella Maris arrived on stage as haunting home movies, religious iconography and glittery gifs popped up on the screen behind them. Part-Haim, part-Heaven’s Gate, the six sisters performed their hits: “Christian electronic dance music” that their late mother, apparently, believed would help them to save the world. The performance was very real, but the band was not. It was a stunt for the Spanish TV mega-hit La Mesías or The Messiah, which was released there in 2023. Its seven episodes centre on an estranged brother and sister, Enric and Irene, who discover that their siblings have become a viral pop band. Cue a soft-focus, flashback-heavy trip into the family’s past, thick with emotional neglect, parental narcissism and religious fanaticism. Oh, and there are UFOs, too. Continue reading...

data.title: Bucking Fastard review – Herzog’s starry twins soap provokes a syncing feeling
data.description: Venice film festival: Rooney and Kate Mara play the real-life Chaplin sisters who spoke in unsettling unison in this silly, pointless drama Werner Herzog is such a unique film-maker that even a dud from him has some interest, but sadly a dud is what this is. It is a fiction feature based on a true story which – despite a few laughs – systematically wastes the audience’s time, as well as the talents of its formidable female leads, real-life sisters Rooney and Kate Mara. You can almost feel this pointless, aimless film making it up as it goes along, losing its way, line by line, scene by scene. It is inspired by the story of twins Freda and Greta Chaplin from York in the UK; they eerily spoke in unison and in the 1980s were the subject of a highly publicised court case for harassing a neighbour. data.title: By Any Means review – Mark Wahlberg and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II drama provokes with horror of 1960s racism
data.description: Elegance Bratton’s civil rights drama in the Jim Crow south confronts you with almost unbearable brutality Black people officially won the unrestricted right to vote in the US in 1965 but many still encountered hurdles on their path to the ballot box: 11 states in the south quickly introduced a poll tax requiring an annual fee to be allowed to vote. The practice unambiguously targeted poor Black communities in an early form of thinly veiled racist voter suppression. Vernon Dahmer wouldn’t stand for it. In January 1966 the Hattiesburg, Mississippi-based Black activist and NAACP chapter head promised to cover the fee for those struggling to afford it. “It’s a proclamation that we here, that we matter,” he says in an early scene in By Any Means, a considered, if blunt, drama inspired by the real-life aftermath of Dahmer’s murder by the Ku Klux Klan. It is Mississippi in the mid-60s and Wayne Strider (a sturdy Yahya Abdul-Mateen II ) is new to the local FBI unit, having recently moved back to his home state from Chicago, and is dealing with bosses who turn a blind eye to racist crimes. “White guys can get away with murder,” says one Black colleague while shaking his head. After his boss receives a message from President Johnson to prioritize the Dahmer murder case, Strider is teamed up with a widely feared mobster, Gregory Scarpa ( Mark Wahlberg with a rather distracting prosthetic nose), who has been shipped in from Brooklyn as part of an off-book mission to track down the Klansmen and bring justice to the killers. Continue reading...

data.title: Chad Powers season two review – Glen Powell’s sweet sports comedy scores a touchdown
data.description: The Hollywood hottie is back as the quarterback in disguise, in an oddball comedy that is naughty, lovable and disarmingly unique In the first episode of season two of Chad Powers, there is but one concern: the main character’s nose has fallen off. The TV outlet for the wacky side of movie hottie Glen Powell, Chad Powers presents itself to us having willingly taken on the burden of a ludicrous premise. Powell is Russ Holliday, a former hotshot college-football quarterback who, eight years ago, committed a career-cancelling faux pas during the televised game that was meant to make him a star. With his sporting dreams suddenly vaporised, he became an obnoxious playboy. But then, just as he felt his feet starting to scrape rock bottom, he heard that a university in Georgia was holding open tryouts for a new quarterback. Donning prosthetic whiskers, teeth, hair and an occasionally unreliable nose – a slightly more sophisticated version of a joke-shop disguise – Russ became “Chad Powers”, a southern oddball and the new star of the team, while constantly dealing with the threat of being found out and sent home. Continue reading...

data.title: Vista, Saarikoski Songs, Three Preludes album review – Saariaho’s iridescent visions evocatively rendered
data.description: Komsi/Nyman/BBC Symphony Orchestra/Oramo (Ondine) Three works by the idiosyncratic Finnish composer who died in 2023 are recorded for the first time Kaija Saariaho died in 2023, leaving behind a significant body of unrecorded music. The three works here, all premiere recordings, span 40 years, yet each bears the Finnish composer’s idiosyncratic fingerprints. The most substantial is Vista (2019), a tone poem inspired by a drive along the scenic Interstate 5 highway to San Diego. The first part, Horizons, opens with a lingering oboe duet before brass, winds and gleaming tuned percussion usher in more piquant colours. This is music on cruise control, with otherworldly washes of strings and a deal of ear-catching incident. Targets, which follows, is altogether more dynamic, a turbulent road trip that winds down to a serene conclusion. Fellow Finn Sakari Oramo is a sensitive, sure-footed guide with the BBC Symphony Orchestra commendably precise and texturally detailed throughout. Continue reading...

data.title: The Gesualdo Six/Colin Currie Group review – surely the year’s most atmospheric Prom
data.description: Royal Albert Hall, London The Gesualdo Six brought focus and luminous tone to a sequence of early devotional music; Reich’s Tehillim made a mesmeric and ecstatic pairing When Steve Reich wrote Tehillim, half his long life ago, it was a very modern contribution to the ancient tradition of psalm singing. In this late-night Prom celebrating Reich’s 90th birthday, Tehillim was presented next to a sequence of devotional music from medieval Europe, making for what was surely one of this year’s most atmospheric Proms. For the first half the stage was held by the singers of the Gesualdo Six, who brought intense focus, luminous tone and consistently outstanding vocal quality to polyphonic works by Machaut, Ockeghem, Dunstable and Josquin des Prez, all sung from memory, interspersed with solo melodies by Pérotin and Hildegard of Bingen. Odd one out, in theory, was a version of Hail Gladdening Light written in 2017 by Owain Park, the Gesualdo Six’s bass and director; but this brief chant-like solo for countertenor, with harmonies filled in by the rest of the singers’ humming, fitted in almost seamlessly. Continue reading...

data.title: Adéla: Prima review – Slovakian star smashes the fourth wall to bask in pop’s cynicism and seduction
data.description: (Polydor) The 22-year-old is impressively frank about indulging industry sleaze in her pursuit of fame on a debut that puts a distinctive spin on the best of 00s hedonism There’s something very striking about hearing a pop star in 2026, their voice larded with Auto-Tune, opening a song with the line “I can’t really sing”. We live in an era where fans seem more aware than ever of the nefarious music business machinations that lurk within the star-making process, one where you’re never far away from online outrage decrying some artist or other as an industry plant. Nevertheless, admitting that the ubiquitous audio processing software is sometimes deployed for a helping hand, not a futuristic aesthetic, feels strangely jarring. On one hand, well of course it is. On the other, actually announcing that without it, you might be honking like a despondent goose, in the first line of a song, still amounts to a dramatic breaking of the fourth wall. That said, it’s very much on brand for Adéla Jergová, who started her career as a contestant on a TV talent show – she failed to make the cut for crumbling “global girl group” Katseye, as documented on Netflix’s Pop Star Academy – before established names alighted on her as a more left-field solo proposition: Grimes co-produced her early single Machine Girl. New artists are well advised to have a USP, something that helps them cut through the mass of peers vying for public attention on streaming services. The 22-year-old Slovakian has chosen to differentiate herself from the serried ranks of post-Brat female pop stars by spiking her songs about hedonism and messy sexual encounters (“no bed frame, we can do it on the carpet … you eat real good for a starving artist”) with a kind of meta commentary on what it is to be a female pop star. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I want to go further’: Justin Broadrick on retiring Godflesh, playing with Phoebe Bridgers – and his new band
data.description: A hernia may mean his screaming days are over, but the Napalm Death alum’s influence on metal echoes on in unexpected places – and with ‘heavy, ugly’ experiments in the pipeline, his passion for ‘outsider music’ remains strong On 4 October 2024, Justin Broadrick felt a pop. The singer and guitarist of pioneering industrial metal duo Godflesh had felt pain in his groin for several years. After a coughing fit following a show in Sofia, Bulgaria, he knew he had a hernia. “It was a small knob in my groin,” says Broadrick. “I got back home and told my partner, and she was like, ‘Let’s watch how it goes.’” He continued to perform live for another year, wearing up to two hernia belts at a time. By the time he got it surgically treated in February this year, it was 13cm long. The next month, Broadrick shared a picture of himself in hospital and announced that Godflesh’s near-four-decade career will soon end. His condition had been caused by the physicality of shouting over their music since he was 18; he just turned 57. If he were to do so again, he would risk blowing out his abdominal wall entirely. There will be two more studio albums – starting with this autumn’s reliably crushing Decay, recorded pre-surgery – and possibly some archival releases and remixes. But beyond that? Nothing. Continue reading...

data.title: An Unexpected Life by Gloria Steinem review – a fitting tribute to a feminist icon
data.description: The activist’s memoir, due to be published this month, now stands as a posthumous testament to her remarkable life Gloria Steinem was due to speak at a women’s lunch in New York at the end of this month and at more events in October, illustrating the central theme of An Unexpected Life, her new memoir, which, when it’s published a few weeks from now, will stand as posthumous testament to the 92-year-old icon: just keep going. So it is, after her death on Wednesday , that the book’s opening pages unfold with a deep, added poignancy and when Steinem expresses gratitude for a life that has been both happier and longer “than I ever imagined”, one is struck by the greater gratitude we probably owe her. An Unexpected Life is a follow-up of sorts to My Life on the Road , the activist’s memoir of a decade ago, and as the tributes pour in, the book offers us an opportunity to go back over Steinem’s hardscrabble origins in Toledo, Ohio, and the roots of her activism. This is where it all happened, the formation of a woman who would come to define second wave feminism by combining a tough-as-they-come stance with something that looked a lot like serenity. Reading the first half of the book, one is reminded of Steinem’s original power and the improbability and iconoclasm of her journey, in which a childhood governed by poverty and dysfunction turned into a lifelong mission to resist the narrow templates laid out for her. Continue reading...

data.title: What we’re reading: Irvine Welsh, Janice Hallett and Guardian readers on the books they enjoyed in August
data.description: Writers and Guardian readers discuss the titles they have read over the last month. Join the conversation in the comments I’ve been enjoying Contrapposto by Dave Eggers. The premise that love and art are the only things that make life worthwhile pulses beautifully through this novel and its two protagonists, spanning decades of their obsession with both, and each other. The tragedy is they are not sufficient alone for a relationship to survive to the exclusion of everything else (namely capitalism, which always has a place at the table), but they remain essential and enduring. Nowhere is this better evoked than here. Think John Williams’s Stoner but with art instead of literature and stuffed with more memorable characters. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Ruin and decay bring a chance of rebirth’: Hidetaka Miyazaki on uniting players in a damaged world
data.description: As FromSoftware’s new multiplayer game The Duskbloods nears release, the legendary game director behind Dark Souls talks connection, pessimism and of course, feet Since 2009’s Demon’s Souls, Japanese video game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has shown the world a different way to think about game design. His games defy convention with punishing fights, obscure rules, and unknowable, inhospitable worlds. The “Soulslike” genre – named after Demon’s Souls and its sequel Dark Souls – is now ubiquitous, influencing multimillion-sellers from God of War and Star Wars: Jedi to Hollow Knight. Miyazaki’s most recent success, 2022’s Elden Ring , which credited Game of Thrones author George RR Martin as a co-creator, sold over 30m copies and inspired Alex Garland to adapt it for the big screen at A24. It earned Miyazaki a spot on Time magazine’s “most influential” list, an accolade he shares with just one other game developer: Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto. Miyazaki is now 51 and has been FromSoftware’s president since 2014, elevated from game designer to CEO after the success of the Souls series. He has a cherubic face that could pass for 35. He rarely speaks publicly, and never on camera. When he does speak, he answers questions like one of his characters – softly, sadly, his head bowed, making eye-contact only when I am speaking. Outside the studio where we speak is the sprawl of Tokyo’s Shinjuku, an ever-changing maze where tourists get lost and pop-up stores appear and vanish without a trace. Today, a J-pop band performs in the square as the cicadas scream from the trees. A gilded statue of Malania, one of Elden Ring’s toughest bosses, looms over this dimly lit conference room inside From’s headquarters, a bonfire checkpoint away from the chaos. Continue reading...

data.title: Martin McDonagh says CIA has ‘done awful things all around the world’
data.description: McDonagh’s new film, Wild Horse Nine, stars John Malkovich as an agent in 1970s Chile who feels ‘guilt and regret’ over his role in global interventions The US’s history of intervening in democratic processes around the world deserves more attention in the light of current political developments, playwright and film-maker Martin McDonagh has said, as his Oscar-tipped film about a rueful CIA agent premieres at the Venice film festival. “I’ve been very interested in the truth of what the CIA has been doing over the last 60 years, and the awful things they’ve done all around the world,” McDonagh said about Wild Horse Nine, his first film since his 2022 tragicomedy The Banshees of Inisherin . “I think maybe something that’s not talked about enough. We know what the KGB are like, but we probably don’t question the CIA’s activity as much as we ought to.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Finally, a victory for the middle-aged white man!’ Chris Cantrill on winning the Edinburgh comedy award
data.description: The ex-marketing manager’s win, for his spoof Sycamore Gap-inspired whodunnit Rewilding, arrives just as he’s gearing up for a new season of hit sketch show SNL UK – which he calls ‘the hardest job of my life’ For the last month, Chris Cantrill has been performing his fringe show Rewilding daily in a lunchtime slot. And yet, when we plan to speak about his victory in the Edinburgh comedy awards , the interview is arranged – on the festival’s penultimate day – for lunchtime. Can he really have won the fringe’s major prize, and – hell of a mic drop, this – immediately sacked off his last two shows? “I couldn’t be happier not to be at the festival today,” he says, on video call from his Northumberland home. But the cancellation, it transpires, is long-standing, because work starts immediately post-fringe on the new series of SNL UK , for which he writes. “But I’m absolutely over the moon not to be doing my show right now,” he admits. “I’ve got a lot of adrenaline in my body slowly seeping out, and I feel like I’ve been hit by a train.” The Edinburgh comedy award (it used to be the Perrier, and was won in the past by Steve Coogan, The League of Gentlemen and Frank Skinner) has been a long time coming for Bradford-born Cantrill. This year’s was his fourth nomination, twice as a solo act, and twice as part of his duo The Delightful Sausage , alongside 2024 winner Amy Gledhill . data.title: Women are giving their partners the ‘Illiterate Boyfriend’ test: ‘Do your best to pronounce these words’
data.description: People online are distressed at men butchering words such as ‘hyperbole’ and ‘hors d’oeuvres’ – highlighting a gender reversal in ‘intelligence gaps’ There are common non-negotiables we look for in a prospective partner. They should be kind, caring and thoughtful. Having a shared interest helps. So does remembering important dates and anniversaries. But how much does it matter if they know how to pronounce the word “gnocchi”? Turns out that’s a potential dealbreaker, at least according to a (rather judgy) cohort on TikTok. See: the “Illiterate Boyfriend” trend, which is testing some couples on the app. Users have compiled a list of what are essentially SAT words for women to ask their male partners to read. Many of these men – this is an overwhelmingly heterosexual activity – fail to finish the list unscathed. They trip over entries such as “hyperbole”, “cynicism”, “diaphragmatic” and the oft-butchered French term, “hors d’oeuvres”. Continue reading...

These bars, with their buttery oat crust, soft fruit filling and crisp, golden topping, are just the sort of thing to have waiting for whenever everyone drifts home. data.title: Jam season is here - bottle that sunshine now to brighten up the winter
data.description: September’s preserving season is a race to capture the heady flavours of summer fruit Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast The ideal time to make lemonade, when lemons are juicy and plentiful and cheap, is in the dead of winter, when the last thing you want is a cooling glass of lemonade. Similarly, jam-making is best done on a grey November afternoon, when the windows are steamed up and the kitchen is the warmest place in the house. Winter is exactly when you want to be standing over a great pot of bubbling fruit and boiling sugar, but much less so in summer, which is when all the good fruit is in season. From May until mid-October, our fruit supplier bills spike exponentially as boxes and boxes of seasonal fruit in its absolute prime make their way to our kitchen for a jam session, and the practice of turning them into a sweet spread is part profession, part obsession. Jam is very much our jam. Early in the season, we can just about cope. The soft fruits start to come in when the weather is still behaving itself, and we love giving them a little seasonal accent – elderflower comes with the last rhubarb, as well as with the first strawberries and apricots, and it pairs wonderfully with all of them (if you are starting there, Felicity Cloake has a very thorough guide to the perfect strawberry jam ). Cherries, meanwhile, go with just about anything, while young bay leaves often find themselves heading into the blackcurrant pot. Fennel fronds and peaches are another favourite, and we make some whenever we can get those two at the same moment. It is an amazing combination: sweet, perfumed and just a little bit green. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: US envoy to visit Kyiv in coming days, Zelenskyy says, as Putin signals ‘chance’ of peace
data.description: Negotiators to visit Kyiv and Moscow as US president Donald Trump says he wants to see an end to the war. What we know on day 1,654 Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that US negotiators will ⁠soon visit Moscow and ⁠Kyiv to resume efforts to end the Russian invasion . The Ukrainian president said in his nightly video address that preliminary dates had been set for the visit. “We expect to see representatives of the US president here in Kyiv,” Zelenskyy said. “There will be a meeting with them in Moscow and in Kyiv. We are ​expecting a meeting with them in the coming days. It is very ‌important. It is important that America continues ‌to be active.” Meanwhile, Vladimir Putin said on Thursday there was a chance of reaching an agreement to end the war in Ukraine . Speaking at an economic ​forum, Russia’s president said a number of countries including the US and China were ready to support a peace settlement. “Ultimately, however, the problem must be resolved by the countries involved in the conflict – Russia ⁠and Ukraine,” he said. “We are grateful to everyone attempting to contribute to a settlement. Is there a chance? In my view, yes, there is.” In Washington, Donald Trump said he wanted to see an end to the war and losses sustained by both sides. “I just want ‌to see that end. I think we’ll get it,” the US president told GB News in an interview that aired on Thursday, a day after telling reporters he wanted a summit with Putin when the Kremlin leader is ready for a peace deal. They last met for US-mediated talks in February. Trump has said he would ask ⁠European nations to pay back the US for military aid and munitions previously sent to Ukraine amid the ongoing war with ⁠Russia and appeared to signal ⁠a halt ​in sales to allied nations. In a social media post, Trump on Thursday also slammed reports of heavily depleted US munition stockpiles amid the ⁠separate war in Iran, while adding that the US was ramping up production and stockpiling munitions. “We are taking them for ourselves, the U.S.A., ⁠rather than selling them to others, but the sales to Allies will soon again, begin,” Trump ​wrote. A Ukrainian strike ⁠on Thursday killed four people, ⁠including two ⁠medical ​personnel, in an attack ⁠on Russia’s border region of Belgorod , officials ⁠said. The region’s official ​headquarters said the ‌dead in Shebekino, just across the border from Ukraine, included a doctor, ‌medic and married couple. ​Three people were injured. Meanwhile, the head of Russian-controlled parts of ⁠eastern Ukraine’s Donetsk Region said ​three ​civilians died in ​drone strikes ‌in ​three ​separate districts of the region. Russian drones struck and damaged a Coca-Cola ⁠plant outside the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Thursday, Zelenskyy said. Officials ⁠said ​there were no injuries in the strike near the town ⁠of Brovary, east of the capital. “Today, the Russians have hit ⁠a Coca-Cola plant with their drone. Coca-Cola ​is such ‌an enemy that ‌they set it on fire ‌with their Shaheds,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address, referring to Iranian-designed drones. “It’s a clear Russian signal to America. The Russians cannot be unaware that ‌this is an American facility.” A Russian attack on ⁠the Ukrainian capital Kyiv ⁠on ​Thursday injured 10 people, triggered a fire and badly damaged a high-rise ⁠residential building , officials said. The city’s military administration initially said one person had died ⁠in the latest assault, but later said ​the report had proved ‌untrue. It said 10 ‌people, including a child, had been hurt. The capital’s mayor, Vitali ‌Klitschko, said nine people were injured, including six medical personnel. Zelenskyy said on Thursday that an investigation would determine what ⁠caused a dispute between two of Ukraine’s security agencies to escalate into a shootout in Kyiv this week that ⁠left ​three members of the defence ministry’s HUR military intelligence directorate injured. The dispute centres on the disappearance ⁠for nine days of a Russian nationalist activist fighting alongside Ukrainian troops. Russia will close German cultural centres on its territory , its foreign minister, Sergey Lavrov, said Thursday in a retaliatory measure reflecting the deepening tensions between Moscow and European countries that are helping Ukraine resist the Kremlin’s invasion. Lavrov’s announcement came after Berlin blamed Moscow for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport on 4 August. Continue reading...

data.title: In 2023, Princeton researchers tested radiative cooling, keeping a building 3.9°C cooler
data.description: Researchers tested a building's ability to stay cooler than outside air naturally.  A special roof released heat towards the sky, while airflow moved air through openings.  This passive system kept the test box significantly cooler than the prevailing outdoor temperature.  The experiment demonstrated radiative cooling working with thermal mass and temperature-driven ventilation.  This approach offers a way to cool buildings without mechanical systems.

data.title: Retired repairman built wind-powered sculptures; his park now draws 194,300 visitors, $5.3 million

data.title: Retrospectiva de Ismael Nery desmonta rótulos sobre artista fora de seu tempo
data.description: "É tudo armadilha. Nery é uma armadilha", diz o curador Yuri Quevedo sobre a produção de Ismael Nery (1900?1934). Seja cubista, surrealista, queer ou modernista, cada tentativa de enquadrar o artista parece levar a um novo desvio em sua obra. É esse movimento que a Pinacoteca de São Paulo coloca em perspectiva a partir deste sábado (5) em "Ismael Nery: Armadilha Moderna", uma das maiores retrospectivas do artista realizadas nos últimos anos, com 230 trabalhos. Leia mais (09/04/2026 - 04h00)

data.title: Combater o crime sem ferir a Constituição
data.description: É de fundamental importância para o futuro do país o debate e o andamento da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que fortalece a participação da União na segurança pública . O núcleo central da PEC, originário do Executivo, tem o objetivo de promover o fortalecimento da cooperação federativa e a constitucionalização do Sistema Único de Segurança Pública, inspirado em modelos bem-sucedidos nas áreas de saúde (SUS) e assistência social (Suas). Como é sabido, o atual texto constitucional não atribui papel relevante à União nem proporciona investimento condizente com as demandas da segurança pública. Ministrar klafsar runt i pågående rättsfall och hänger ut medier och journalister som vågar sig på granskning. Det är ett fräckt angrepp på den fria åsiktsbildningen, skriver yttrandefrihetsexperten Nils Funcke.

data.title: Falska rykten spreds efter dödsfall i Karlstad
data.description: Två män i 20-årsåldern misstänks för att ha misshandlat en 48-årig pappa som senare dog av sina skador. Efter händelsen har falska rykten spridits om att de misstänkta männen ska ha utländsk bakgrund. Sverigedemokraten Charlie Weimers var en av politikerna som uppmärksammat fallet. – Jag står för varje ord jag skrev, säger han.

data.title: Övergången skedde utan prövning – nu vill boende få hyrorna granskade
data.description: När presumtionstiden gick ut för några av kommunala Familjebostäders hus i Stockholm fördes hyrorna in i bruksvärdessystemet – utan någon prövning. data.title: Högt mål trots motgångarna: Ska bli ett europeiskt storlag
data.description: Med den internationella ägargruppen Crux i ryggen har FC Rosengård inlett en total förvandling. Målet är att bli ett europeiskt storlag – men starten har kantats av oväntade motgångar i damallsvenskan. Ändå känner klubben sig starkare än någonsin. – Det här är en nystart där vi bygger allt från grunden. Vi är en startup, säger fotbollsbolagets styrelseordförande Jenny Damgaard.

data.title: Läckt polisrapport om händelserna i Ceuta sätter press på Sánchez

data.title: Oscar Kazanelson: 25 lat ROBYG to historia ludzi, zaufania i konsekwentnego rozwoju
data.description: ROBYG od ponad 25 lat współtworzy polski rynek mieszkaniowy. Dziś grupa jest jednym z największych deweloperów w kraju, działa w siedmiu miastach, zrealizowała ponad 38 tys. mieszkań i stworzyła miejsca do życia dla ponad 100 tys. mieszkańców. Powrót na Giełdę Papierów Wartościowych w 2026 r.otworzył nowy etap rozwoju spółki. O filozofii „miast w mieście”, ludziach, którzy budują sukces ROBYG, oraz planach na przyszłość rozmawiamy z Oscarem Kazanelsonem, przewodniczącym rady nadzorczej ROBYG.

data.title: Sucho odhalilo na dně Orlíku rezavé sudy. Lidem se vybavují vraždy, volají policii
data.description: Klesající hladina orlické přehrady odhaluje v bahně a písku i zrezavělé sudy. Lidé si ještě dobře pamatují na sérii brutálních, tzv. Orlických vražd ze začátku 90. let. data.title: Tisíc a jedna grimasa. Meloniová slaví, její kabinet vládne nejdéle od Mussoliniho
data.description: Vláda italské premiérky Giorgie Meloniové se stala nejdéle sloužícím kabinetem v historii republikánské Itálie. To znamená od roku 1946. data.title: Čakovický prak a pramen, který nevytryskl. Druhá řada Stop Járy Cimrmana už vzniká
data.description: Téměř tři desítky míst napříč Českem, která odkazují k působení fiktivního českého génia, představí druhá řada cestopisného cyklu Stopy Járy Cimrmana. Průvodce Miroslav Táborský se v šesti nových dílech, které Česká televize odvysílá příští rok na jaře, setká nejen se svými hereckými kolegy z Divadla Járy Cimrmana, ale také s místními nadšenci, kteří mistrovu stopu připomínají veřejnosti.

data.description: Ve Fakultní nemocnici Motol a Homolka v Praze ve čtvrtek odpoledne hořelo. Nikdo se nezranil, ale muselo se evakuovat 18 pacientů. Oheň zasáhl opláštění onkologického centra, škoda činí asi 30 milionů korun. Informovali o tom mluvčí pražských hasičů Miroslav Řezáč a mluvčí nemocnice Martina Dostálová.

data.title: Arménie by se nebránila odchodu ruských vojáků. Odejdeme klidně zítra, tvrdí Putin
data.description: Arménie nepovažuje přítomnost ruské vojenské základny na svém území za „životně důležitou“. Pokud by se ji Moskva rozhodla opustit, Jerevan by tomu nebránil, sdělil arménský premiér Nikol Pašinjan. data.title: Nerada mluvila o své nemoci, říká Štefan Margita při křtu knihy o Haně Zagorové
data.description: V pražském Divadle Kalich slavnostně pokřtili knihu k nedožitým 80. narozeninám zpěvačky Hany Zagorové. Kmotrem se stal operní pěvec a manžel zesnulé zpěvačky Štefan Margita. K slavnostnímu aktu se připojil též křest narozeninového výběru 80 hitů z její téměř 60 let dlouhé hudební kariéry. Poprvé před publikem došlo i na ukázky z připravovaného muzikálu Biograf láska 2, které divadlo uvede 6. září.

data.title: OBRAZEM: Letadlovka Abraham Lincoln při návratu šokovala svým vzhledem
data.description: Když americká letadlová loď Abraham Lincoln ve středu zakotvila v přístavu jižně od thajského Bangkoku, mnohé lidi šokoval její vzhled. Plavidlo je totiž od přídě až po záď pokryté korozí. Ač je to podle odborníků normální, je potřeba ji odstranit. Její výskyt totiž může pro plavidlo představovat ohrožení. Je to z další z jevů, které vedle zhoršené morálky posádky vnější svět na válečné lodi zaujaly.

data.title: Macinka bez ochranky u muže v kukle. Nachytal se partou trollů, nechápe opozice
data.description: Internetem se šíří snímek z videa, na němž ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka sedí u rozhovoru s mužem v kukle. Měl jím být anonym vystupující pod přezdívkou Thomas Paukner, jenže podle skupiny Detektivní Parta ministr pohořel v bezpečnostním experimentu. Do studia údajně dorazil bez ochranky a ocitl se v blízkosti maket zbraní i atrapy výbušniny. Macinka nařčení odmítá. Jeho počínání kritizuje opozice.

data.title: EU official says it’s not time to ‘normalize’ Russia at G20 finance talks
data.description:
ASHEVILLE: EU economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis said Tuesday that it is not the time to “normalize” Moscow’s presence at G20 meetings as European leaders pushed back against the Russian finance minister’s attendance at ongoing talks.
	“I think the European position is known,” Dombrovskis told reporters on the sidelines of the US-hosted finance leaders’ gathering in Asheville, North Carolina.
	“We do not think now is the time to normalize Russia” or its presence at such talks, the Latvian official said.

data.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill three in operation to seize Hamas figure: officials
data.description:
GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Heavy Israeli bombardment killed three people in Gaza City on Tuesday, Palestinian health officials said, in what both sides described as an Israeli-backed ground operation to seize a senior Hamas figure.

	Eyewitnesses reported around a dozen strikes on Tuesday morning in western Gaza City, where the territory’s civil defense agency said three people were killed, including two children and a woman.

data.title: ‘Massive’ Russian missile, drone attack on Kyiv kills 8
data.description:
KYIV: A “massive” Russian attack killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, including seven at a railways depot, officials said Tuesday, as Moscow pressed its air campaign on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas.
	The strikes came as children were set to return to school after summer holidays and as authorities tightened security measures following weeks of intensified Russian attacks on the capital.

data.title: World leaders need to see rising oceans in Pacific: UN official
data.description:
KOROR: Leaders from the world's top economies should stand on a Pacific atoll to see the reality of record sea level rise, a top UN official said in Palau on Monday.

	Noting last week's deadly floods in Nepal, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed said rising seas in the Pacific were the "other side of that story".

	"We do already know that a warming climate is changing the world's ice at extraordinary speeds, not only threatening the communities below glaciers but adding more water to our oceans," she told reporters.

data.description: La advertencia del científico brasileño coincide con un informe publicado este mismo jueves por la Organización Meteorológica Mundial, que confirma que el fenómeno alcanzará una intensidad muy fuerte en los próximos meses, incrementando el riesgo de episodios climáticos extremos, sequías prolongadas y olas de calor en diversas regiones del planeta.

data.title: Yango Cameroun poursuit son partenariat sécurité avec Douala et Yaoundé, confirme une nouvelle session de formation des chauffeurs en Septembre
data.description: © DR Le nouveau Rapport Yango Ride sur la Sécurité 2024–2025 relie les progrès en matière de sécurité, à l'échelle régionale, à la modernisation des technologies de confidentialité, aux systèmes anti-fraude et à l'assistance d'urgence disponible 24h/24 et 7j/7 — renforcés au Cameroun par des programmes conjoints de formation des chauffeurs et de bilans de santé avec les autorités locales. Douala, Cameroun — 3 septembre 2026 Yango Ride, service de VTC appartenant au groupe technologique mondial Yango Group, a publié aujourd'hui les résultats régionaux de son Rapport sur la Sécurité 2024–2025, qui détaille les technologies et dispositifs d'assistance mis en place pour rendre la mobilité plus sûre pour les passagers et les chauffeurs partenaires à travers l'Afrique, y compris au Cameroun. En juillet 2025, Yango s'est associé aux mairies de Douala et de Yaoundé pour organiser deux événements dédiés à la sécurité et au bien-être des chauffeurs, réunissant plus de 100 chauffeurs partenaires dans les deux villes. Chaque session a combiné une formation sur les fonctionnalités de sécurité intégrées à l'application et des bilans de santé gratuits pour les chauffeurs partenaires, favorisant un dialogue direct entre les chauffeurs, les autorités municipales et les experts en sécurité de Yango. Yango a confirmé qu'un événement similaire consacré à la sécurité et au bien-être des chauffeurs sera de nouveau organisé en septembre 2026, prolongeant ainsi la portée du programme au Cameroun. Les événements organisés au Cameroun s'inscrivent dans une dynamique continentale plus large. Sur la période 2024–2025, le déploiement de nouvelles mesures d'analyse du style de conduite et de contrôle de la vitesse a permis une baisse de 38 % des incidents de conduite dangereuse signalés à l'échelle de la région Afrique, passant de 13,05 à 8,08 incidents par million de trajets. Des baisses comparables ont été enregistrées en Côte d'Ivoire (35 %), en Zambie (49 %), en Angola (34 %) et au Sénégal (33 %) — le même dispositif de sécurité qui encadre aujourd'hui les activités de Yango au Cameroun. Avec la poursuite du déploiement des technologies de protection de la confidentialité des appels, les réclamations liées à des contacts après course ont également reculé dans plusieurs marchés africains : -11 % en Côte d'Ivoire, -22 % en Angola, -8 % au Sénégal et -4 % en Zambie. L'assistance d'urgence est disponible 24h/24 et 7j/7 sur l'ensemble des marchés où Yango opère, y compris au Cameroun : la technologie permet d'identifier les demandes urgentes, tandis que des spécialistes formés restent responsables de l'analyse des situations et des décisions à prendre. Dans 90 % des cas urgents à l'échelle mondiale, un spécialiste formé vise à établir un premier contact en moins de 5 minutes Une technologie présente à chaque étape de la course Ces résultats reflètent un dispositif de sécurité qui intervient avant, pendant et après chaque course sur la plateforme Yango, y compris au Cameroun. Avant le début d'une course, la vérification de l'identité et des documents — comprenant le contrôle du permis de conduire, des selfies de vérification récurrents et des systèmes anti-fraude — détermine qui peut accéder au service. Pendant la course, passagers et chauffeurs partenaires peuvent accéder à un Centre de Sécurité leur permettant de partager leur itinéraire avec des contacts de confiance, de joindre l'assistance d'urgence en cas de conflit, et d'utiliser le bouton SOS pour contacter les services d'urgence locaux. L'analyse du style de conduite et la surveillance GPS de la vitesse permettent d'identifier les comportements à risque répétés et de déclencher une réponse proportionnée, de l'avertissement jusqu'au retrait de la plateforme. Après chaque course, chauffeur partenaire et passager ont la possibilité de s'évaluer mutuellement, ce qui alimente leur profil. Les appels via l'application permettent de garder les échanges dans des canaux protégés, sans qu'aucune des deux parties n'ait à partager son numéro personnel. « Une baisse de 38 % des incidents de conduite dangereuse à travers l'Afrique n'est pas le fruit d'une seule fonctionnalité ou d'une solution propre à un marché : c'est le résultat d'une technologie appliquée de façon cohérente, combinée à l'expertise et à la connaissance du terrain de nos équipes dans chaque pays. Ce même dispositif s'applique avant, pendant et après chaque course, partout où nous opérons, et ce type de résultats est la raison pour laquelle nous continuons d'investir dans la prévention, la détection et l'assistance, afin d'offrir une meilleure expérience à l'ensemble de nos utilisateurs », — Roman Karlash, Directeur Général de Yango Ride Au-delà de l'application : des partenariats avec les autorités locales au Cameroun Au Cameroun, le dispositif de sécurité de Yango va au-delà de l'application grâce à des partenariats directs avec les institutions publiques. Douala, Cameroun — 3 septembre 2026 Yango Ride, service de VTC appartenant au groupe technologique mondial Yango Group, a publié aujourd'hui les résultats régionaux de son Rapport sur la Sécurité 2024–2025, qui détaille les technologies et dispositifs d'assistance mis en place pour rendre la mobilité plus sûre pour les passagers et les chauffeurs partenaires à travers l'Afrique, y compris au Cameroun. Chaque session a combiné une formation sur les fonctionnalités de sécurité intégrées à l'application et des bilans de santé gratuits pour les chauffeurs partenaires, favorisant un dialogue direct entre les chauffeurs, les autorités municipales et les experts en sécurité de Yango. data.title: Yaoundé : l’Hôpital Central célèbre la kinésithérapie et la lutte contre les AVC
data.description: © DR Du 1er au 8 septembre 2026, l'Hôpital Central de Yaoundé organise une semaine dédiée à la kinésithérapie avec bilans gratuits et symposium sur les maladies cardiovasculaires et les AVC, pour promouvoir l'accès aux soins et la rééducation fonctionnelle. Depuis le 1er septembre 2026, l'Hôpital Central de Yaoundé célèbre la kinésithérapie à travers une série d'activités sanitaires et scientifiques qui se poursuivent jusqu'au 8 septembre prochain. Jusqu'au 7 septembre, l'établissement propose aux populations des bilans et prises en charge kinésithérapiques gratuits. Une initiative forte dans un contexte où l'accès aux soins de rééducation reste un défi pour de nombreux Camerounais. Selon Élysée Mvondo, Major du Service de Physio-Kinésithérapie, cette campagne vise à faciliter l'accès aux soins, à sensibiliser sur l'importance de la rééducation et à mettre en lumière le rôle essentiel des kinésithérapeutes dans la récupération fonctionnelle et l'autonomie des patients, notamment après un accident vasculaire cérébral (AVC). Le point d'orgue est prévu le 8 septembre, à l'occasion de la Journée internationale de la kinésithérapie. Un symposium consacré aux « maladies cardiovasculaires et aux AVC » clôturera la semaine. Ce rendez-vous scientifique réunit médecins, kinésithérapeutes et infirmiers autour de la prévention, de la prise en charge et de la rééducation de ces pathologies, première cause de handicap acquis. À travers cette mobilisation, l'Hôpital Central de Yaoundé réaffirme son engagement en faveur de soins accessibles et de qualité, conformément à sa devise : « Service – Qualité – Probité ». Cet article Yaoundé : l’Hôpital Central célèbre la kinésithérapie et la lutte contre les AVC est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Présidentielle 2025 : Denis Emilien Atangana se félicite d’avoir évité le pire en refusant 100 millions pour investir Maurice Kamto
data.description: © (DR) Dans une publication sur ses réseaux sociaux, le président du Front des démocrates camerounais (FDC) considère le MRC comme une Organisation non gouvernementale ‘’incapable de s’autogérer’’. Près d'un an après l'élection présidentielle de 2025 au Cameroun, Denis Emilien Atangana se félicite d'avoir refusé l'investiture au candidat recalé Maurice Kamto moyennant une offre de 100 millions de francs CFA. Le président du FDC fait ce jeudi une brève publication illustrée pour affirmer que le refus de 100 millions lui a permis "de rester en vie et de poursuivre le vrai combat du changement et non du remplacement". L'homme politique évoque la vie en faisant référence à la mort de Christian Penda Ekoka, de Paul Eric Kingue et d’Anicet Ekane. Des acteurs politiques d'influence qui sont décédés après avoir cheminé avec le Pr. Maurice Kamto pendant des moments sensibles de la vie politique nationale. Face aux critiques et en remontant l'histoire récente, Denis Emilien Atangana démontre par ailleurs dans une autre publication que son parti le FDC est au-dessus du MRC. D'après lui, le MRC n'est qu'un « Groupe de pression communautaire » comparé au FDC qui est "un parti politique sérieux" présent au sein des institutions. Cependant, le sérieux de ce parti est souvent remis en question par l'opposition qui reconnaît au FDC une proximité coupable avec le régime et avec le parti au pouvoir. Son leader a été l'un des premiers responsables politiques à féliciter le président Paul Biya pour sa réélection en octobre 2025. Aussi, les sorties successives du leader du parti au moment où le MRC est à couteau tiré avec le ministre de l'Administration territoriale suscitent des interrogations. Elles tendent à confirmer la thèse selon laquelle le FDC est l'une des créations du système gouvernant destinée à fragiliser des partis qui se montrent virulents dans leur opposition contre le pouvoir. Cet article Présidentielle 2025 : Denis Emilien Atangana se félicite d’avoir évité le pire en refusant 100 millions pour investir Maurice Kamto est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Réforme foncière : le MINDCAF passe à l’action
data.description: © DR Le 1er septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, le ministre Henri Eyebe Ayissi a présidé les assises spéciales sur la réforme foncière, annonçant l'application immédiate des lettres-circulaires 2024-2026 et la lettre-circulaire n°0005 du 31 août dernier sur les Commissions consultatives. Le Conseil régional du Centre a abrité le 1er septembre 2026, les assises spéciales consacrées au lancement officiel des lettres-circulaires et instructions ministérielles 2024-2026 pour la gouvernance foncière. Présidée par le ministre des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires Foncières, Henri Eyebe Ayissi, la rencontre a réuni autorités administratives, chefs traditionnels et acteurs de la chaîne foncière. Le ministre a rappelé les limites de l'ordonnance de 1974 face à la pression démographique, l'urbanisation et les contentieux, et justifié la réforme engagée dans le cadre de la SND30 et des directives de la FAO. Deux annonces majeures : la signature de la Lettre-Circulaire n°0005 du 31 août 2026 fixant les modalités de désignation des notables au sein des Commissions Consultatives, et une évaluation rigoureuse lors du débat parlementaire sur le futur projet de loi foncier. Le MINDCAF a prescrit l'application stricte et immédiate : fichier annuel actualisé des attestations des chefferies de 3e degré, barèmes de descente des commissions et soumission de tous les dossiers en cours aux nouvelles règles, sous peine de sanctions. Cet article Réforme foncière : le MINDCAF passe à l’action est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: KOAFEC 2026 : L’IA au cœur du partenariat Corée-Afrique à Séoul
data.description: © DR Du 8 au 11 septembre à Séoul, la 8e Conférence ministérielle Corée-Afrique (KOAFEC) se penche sur le numérique. En jeu : 1 000 milliards de dollars de PIB supplémentaires que l'IA pourrait apporter à l'Afrique d'ici 2035. L'Intelligence artificielle au coeur des enjeux. Du 8 au 11 septembre 2026, Séoul accueille la 8e Conférence ministérielle sur la coopération économique Corée-Afrique (KOAFEC) à l'hôtel Grand Walkerhill. Co-organisée par le Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement, le ministère coréen des Finances et de l'Économie et la Banque coréenne d'import-export, la rencontre est placée sous le thème « Exploiter l'IA et les infrastructures numériques pour la transformation de l'Afrique ». L'événement réunit décideurs politiques africains et coréens, partenaires de développement, investisseurs et leaders des start-up pour explorer comment la technologie peut accélérer une croissance inclusive et durable. Le potentiel est immense : l'intelligence artificielle pourrait ajouter jusqu'à 1 000 milliards de dollars au PIB africain d'ici 2035. Le débat portera sur les conditions pour saisir cette opportunité : infrastructures, compétences, systèmes énergétiques, connectivité et politiques adaptées. Cet article KOAFEC 2026 : L’IA au cœur du partenariat Corée-Afrique à Séoul est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: PME : Douala accueille la 11e Caravane des CGA
data.description: © DR Organisée par le MINPMEESA les 1er et 2 septembre 2026 à Douala, la 11e édition de la Caravane de sensibilisation pour l'adhésion aux Centres de Gestion Agréés a mobilisé l'écosystème entrepreneurial autour de la formalisation et de la compétitivité des PME. Douala a abrité les 1er et 2 septembre 2026, la 11e édition des Caravanes de sensibilisation des PME pour leur adhésion aux Centres de Gestion Agréés (CGA). Placée sous le thème « Optimisation du dispositif d'accompagnement des entrepreneurs dans les CGA : défis, stratégies et perspectives », cette initiative du Ministère des PME, de l'Économie Sociale et de l'Artisanat vise à rapprocher les entrepreneurs des dispositifs d'accompagnement pour favoriser formalisation, gouvernance et pérennisation. Au cœur des échanges : avantages liés à l'adhésion aux CGA, obligations comptables et fiscales, nouvelles mesures de la Loi de finances 2026, réforme de la fiscalité locale et Impôt Général Synthétique, accès au financement et accompagnement des jeunes et femmes entrepreneurs. L'écosystème était mobilisé : administrations, DGI, structures d'appui, patronat, banques, chambres consulaires, CGA et partenaires techniques. Objectif : sensibiliser 5 000 acteurs. La caravane s'est déployée à travers un village des CGA, une caravane mobile dans la ville et des descentes chez un jeune et une femme entrepreneure. Depuis 2016, le MINPMEESA poursuit cette dynamique à travers le pays. Cet article PME : Douala accueille la 11e Caravane des CGA est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Budget-Programme : la CEMAC passe à l’action
data.description: © DR Sous la présidence du Vice-Président de la Commission, un atelier de trois jours s'est ouvert le 02 septembre 2026 à la Représentation de la CEMAC à Yaoundé pour l'appropriation du Plan Stratégique 2027-2030 et du Budget-Programme, une étape décisive pour l'intégration régionale. Une étape décisive pour l'avenir de l'intégration en Afrique Centrale. La Représentation de la Commission de la CEMAC à Yaoundé accueille pendant trois jours un atelier stratégique de haut niveau. Placés sous la présidence du Vice-Président de la Commission, les travaux visent à doter l'institution d'instruments de gouvernance modernes et performants. L'objectif est triple : permettre aux membres du Gouvernement de la Commission de s'approprier le Plan Stratégique 2027-2030 et le dispositif du Budget-Programme, examiner et valider leurs orientations fondamentales, puis approuver la feuille de route opérationnelle avant sa transmission au Conseil des Ministres. Pendant 72 heures, les réflexions s'intensifient autour du renforcement de la gouvernance financière, de la performance institutionnelle et de l'impact direct des politiques communautaires au service des populations de la zone CEMAC. Cet article Budget-Programme : la CEMAC passe à l’action est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : la Banque mondiale finance 1 000 jeunes promoteurs d’entreprises en phase de démarrage
data.description: © (DR) Les bénéficiaires sont recrutés dans le cadre du deuxième cycle du Programme de concours des plans d'affaires du Projet filets sociaux adaptatifs et d'inclusion économique. Au total 1000 jeunes promoteurs d'entreprises âgés de 18 à 35 ans et établis à Yaoundé, Douala, Buea, Bamenda, Maroua et Garoua vont bénéficier des appuis financiers pour renforcer le démarrage de leurs projets d'entreprise. Le gouvernement vient de lancer les inscriptions en ligne des candidatures au deuxième cycle du Programme de concours des plans d'affaires du Projet filets sociaux adaptatifs et d'inclusion économique. Ledit projet bénéficie de l'appui technique et financier de la Banque mondiale. Le but est d'améliorer les conditions de vie des ménages défavorisées et les plus démunis et de promouvoir l'inclusion économique et l'entrepreneuriat des jeunes. Pour ce deuxième cycle, les entreprises concernées sont celles qui sont en phase de démarrage, d'une existence d'un à trois ans, étant formelles ou informelles. L'autre critère est que ces entreprises doivent présenter un potentiel de croissance significatif et un potentiel de création d'emplois dans les secteurs porteurs et prioritaires pour le gouvernement. Le Programme de concours des plans d'affaires est doté d'une enveloppe globale de 5,5 milliards de francs CFA. Grâce à cette enveloppe, les entreprises retenues vont bénéficier d'un appui financier, des formations entrepreneuriales, des séances de coaching ainsi que d'un suivi après financement leur permettant de renforcer leur compétitivité et leur pérennité. Derrière ce programme se cache aussi la volonté du gouvernement de favoriser la création d'emplois durables, de stimuler l'innovation, de renforcer la compétitivité des Petites et moyennes entreprises et de contribuer à la croissance économique. Les candidats peuvent soumettre leurs dossiers sur le plateforme via l'adresse https://www.pfs-aie.cm/public/portail/cpa entre le 07 septembre et le 17 octobre 2026. Cet article Cameroun : la Banque mondiale finance 1 000 jeunes promoteurs d’entreprises en phase de démarrage est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ formation professionnelle : les frais de scolarité réduits de moitié pour les personnes vivant avec un handicap
data.description: © (DR) Un arrêté conjoint des ministres de la Formation professionnelle Mounouna Foutsou, des Finances Louis Paul Motaze et des Affaires sociales Pauline Irène Nguene, précise les modalités d'application de cette mesure. Les personnes vivant avec un handicap et désireuses d'acquérir une formation professionnelle dans un établissement public sont bénéficiaires de la réduction de 50% des frais de scolarité. Cette réduction s'applique directement sur le montant des frais exigibles et mentionnée sur la quittance de paiement. La mesure s'applique dans toutes les structures publiques offrant des formations professionnelles peu importe le secteur. Pour en profiter, certaines conditions sont à remplir. L'arrêté conjoint oblige les potentiels bénéficiaires à justifier d'un taux d'incapacité potentielle permanente d'au moins 50%. Le texte indique aussi qu'il faut être titulaire d'une carte nationale d'invalidité, en cours de validité, délivrée par le ministère en charge des Affaires sociales ; être régulièrement inscrit au fichier national des personnes handicapées auprès du ministère en charge des Affaires sociales. Il faut enfin être régulièrement admis et inscrit dans un établissement public de formation professionnelle. Une fois que ces conditions cumulatives sont remplies, le candidat peut adresser la demande de réduction des frais de scolarité au chef de l'établissement concerné. Celui-ci délivre une attestation à présenter au moment du paiement. La délivrance de ladite attestation est soumise à la constitution d'un dossier comprenant une demande manuscrite adressée au chef du centre. Une copie de la carte nationale d'invalidité. Une copie de l'acte de naissance. Une copie de la carte nationale d'identité. Tout document attestant de l'admission ou de la pré-inscription. D'un rapport d'enquête sociale le cas échéant. La réduction de moitié des frais de scolarité s'ajoute à d'autres mesures facilitant l'accès à l'éducation et à la formation professionnelle des personnes handicapées. Le décret du Premier ministre du 26 juillet 2018 prévoit une aide à l'éducation et à la formation professionnelle à cette catégorie de personnes. À titre illustratif, il prévoit l'exemption totale ou partielle des frais scolaires et universitaires, l'octroi des bourses, l'octroi des subventions pour l'achat des équipements didactiques au profit des personnes handicapées indigentes. Cet article Cameroun/ formation professionnelle : les frais de scolarité réduits de moitié pour les personnes vivant avec un handicap est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Baleine échouée à Muanda : des experts saluent le projet d’exhumation pour la recherche scientifique
data.description: L’exhumation de la baleine échouée à Muanda, dans le Kongo-Central, devrait permettre aux experts de poursuivre les études scientifiques sur cet animal, neuf semaines après son enfouissement. Des spécialistes de l’environnement ont salué mercredi 3 septembre, la décision annoncée par la ministre de l’Environnement, tout en appelant au respect des normes sanitaires et environnementales.

data.title: Déraillement du train urbain de Kinshasa, 15 jours après sa reprise
data.description: À Kinshasa, le train urbain n'a pas fonctionné ce jeudi 3 septembre 2026 matin. L’engin a déraillé mercredi soir sur le chemin de son retour dans la commune de Masina, soit quinze jours après sa reprise. Cet incident ravive les craintes sur l'état d'une infrastructure vieillissante dont dispose l'Office national des transports (ONTRA).

data.title: La TikTokeuse Denise Dusauchoy placée sous mandat d’arrêt provisoire en RDC
data.description: La TikTokeuse Denise Dusauchoy (Denise Mukendi) a été placée sous mandat d’arrêt provisoire après avoir été présentée, mercredi 2 septembre, au ministère public, selon des sources judiciaires. Elle fait l’objet de poursuites pour plusieurs faits susceptibles de constituer des infractions au regard de la législation congolaise. D’après les mêmes sources, elle est notamment soupçonnée de faire, sur les réseaux sociaux, l’apologie des activités subversives des rebelles de la coalition AFC/M23.

data.title: Plus de 900 000 enfants attendus pour la vaccination contre la polio à Kisangani
data.description: La province de la Tshopo déploie une campagne de riposte vaccinale en porte-à-porte du jeudi 3 au samedi 5 septembre, ciblant plus de 924 000 enfants âgés de 0 à 59 mois. data.title: The Inconvenient Truth: Democracy does not fail in The Chamber, it fails in the Committee Room
data.description: There is a comfortable illusion that nations take from their chambers, the polished benches, the ceremonial mace, the eloquence of debate broadcast to the world. It is tempting to believe that this is where a country's political governance truly lives, and truly dies. Yet the uncomfortable truth is that democracy's real test rarely unfolds in full view. It unfolds quietly, in modest rooms, before smaller audiences, where the difficult questions are either genuinely asked or conveniently avoided. Parliaments across the world function, in broad governance terms, like giant public boardrooms: they deliberate, legislate, scrutinise executive action and represent citizens. But as in any serious organisation, the effectiveness of the larger governing body depends heavily on the quality of its committees. The grand chamber may hold constitutional authority, but committees provide the depth, specialised scrutiny and early warning that make that authority effective. When committees work, democracy sees further. When they become ceremonial, partisan or technically weak, the national boardroom begins governing with blurred vision.
